title: Improving NL→Formal-Spec Semantic Correctness via Constrained Prompting plus Verifier Feedback (Preregistered, Repair)
research_question: Does combining constrained prompting with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase the semantic-correctness rate of translating operator natural-language intents into formal network specifications compared to baseline prompting?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: Constrained prompting (structured templates + explicit semantic slots) increases NL→formal-spec semantic-correctness versus unconstrained baseline prompting.
H2: Adding deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback (generate→verify→repair) further increases semantic-correctness versus constrained prompting alone.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: Which intent types (reachability, isolation, ACL, QoS) benefit most from verifier feedback and how do revision counts vary by type?
EQ2: What common syntactic or semantic failure modes remain after verifier-feedback repair?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic, programmatically generated operator intents covering four intent families: reachability, isolation, ACL-change, QoS constraint.
Topology sizes restricted to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes) generated deterministically by the preregistered topology generator.
Confirmatory claims are strictly about performance on the sampled synthetic intent corpus and verifier-harness; no claim of production-network generalization is made.
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: N=150 distinct synthetic intents programmatically generated (target balance: 50 per intent family after deterministic pre-filters). For each intent, execute three translation conditions conceptually (A: baseline free-text prompt, B: constrained template prompt, C: constrained prompt + verifier-feedback loop) but the supplied execution adapter implements the paired baseline vs guarded episodes with one shared initial candidate per task (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Per-adapter constraints: exactly one initial model generation per task (shared across conditions) and at most one additional guarded repair call if the verifier fails the initial candidate, for a maximum of two model calls per task. Each model call runs in a fresh isolated API session with state reset; runtime sampling parameters for each call are recorded in the model-configuration metadata (no claim of fixed random seed or deterministic sampling is made). Inclusion rule: intents flagged as ambiguous by the preregistered rule-based ambiguity detector are excluded from the confirmatory set and routed to the exploratory corpus before any model call. Exclusion rules (parser failures, unsupported verifier features) are applied deterministically prior to model calls. Randomization: none required (paired within-intent analysis). All intent IDs, topology seeds, and per-call runtime sampling parameters will be published.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: detect an absolute increase of 15 percentage points (e.g., baseline 35% → guarded 50%) with ~80% power at alpha=0.05 (two-sided). Calculation method: approximate paired-proportion power calculation (McNemar-style) under conservative discordant-pair proportion ≈0.30; analytical result ≈132, rounded to N=150 for buffer. Sensitivity analyses: recompute power under baseline rates 25%–45% and discordant rates 0.20–0.40 via bootstrap simulation. Recommended scenario: N=150 (planned model calls consistent with execution contract maximum_model_calls = 300).
exclusion_rules: Ambiguity-detection true: exclude intent from confirmatory set and route to exploratory corpus (deterministic, pre-model-call).
Parser mapping failure to verifier input: exclude from confirmatory set and record as 'parse_failure'.
Verifier reports 'unsupported-feature' for an intent: exclude deterministically and record reason code.
missingness_plan: Model/API timeouts or parsing failures are logged and trigger deterministic retry policy: one automatic retry after fixed backoff; if still failing, mark the model-call as failed. For the primary analysis incomplete intent-condition pairs are removed (complete_pair_primary). Sensitivity analysis treats failed guarded outputs as failures (zero) and reports results. All failed-call counts, causes, and hashes are published.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired binary comparison of semantic-correctness (verifier pass/fail) between the guarded condition (C) and baseline (A) using the registered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor (McNemar-style paired-proportion approach with bootstrap confidence intervals). Primary estimand id used: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Report absolute percentage-point differences, odds ratios, exact two-sided p-values, and 95% bootstrap CIs computed with 10,000 bootstrap resamples. Secondary analyses: paired tests B vs A and C vs B with Bonferroni correction across these two secondary contrasts (each α=0.025 two-sided). For condition C report median and IQR of revision iterations. Missing/incomplete pairs: primary treatment is 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude incomplete pairs); sensitivity analysis 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' treats failed/missing guarded outputs as failures (zero). All analysis code, seeds (analysis-side PRNG seeds), and raw verifier verdicts are published.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test: single primary contrast (C vs A) at α=0.05 two-sided. Two secondary confirmatory contrasts (B vs A and C vs B) corrected via Bonferroni (each at α=0.025 two-sided). All other subgroup and error-taxonomy analyses are explicitly labeled exploratory and not used for confirmatory claims.

stopping_rule: Process all N=150 confirmatory intents to completion unless pre-execution unit-tests for mapping/verifier fail (abort run). No early stopping for statistical significance; runs stop when all confirmatory tasks complete or when a deterministic abort condition (unit-test failure, mapping-code failure) occurs.
